title: Console navigation reorg: streamlined sidebar, route semantics, and workspace switcher UX
creator: Asha Patel
description: High-level redesign of Redwood Console information architecture focusing on: 1) a condensed, role-aware left sidebar; 2) clearer top-level routing and deep-links for dashboards, rollouts, and cost views; and 3) a discoverable workspace switcher pattern that supports cross-workspace user flows and SSO guests. This ticket captures prototypes, review feedback, acceptance criteria, and next steps toward shipping the new nav in console-2026.04.
motivation: Users struggle to find per-model dashboards and rollout controls when teams have multiple workspaces. The current sidebar is cluttered and makes routing unpredictable for deep links and browser history. We aim to reduce navigation noise, improve task completion for engineers and PMs, and enable stable deep-links for observability and incident workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Left sidebar shows a maximum of 7 primary entries with ability to expand secondary items
Workspace switcher available from header and sidebar with quick-search; switching preserves last-used route in target workspace where permissible
Deep-linkable routes for: /workspaces/:id/dashboards, /workspaces/:id/rollouts/:id, /workspaces/:id/costs and stable query params for filters
Keyboard shortcut (cmd+k) opens global quick navigation with fuzzy search across routes and resources
ARIA-compliant sidebar interactions (role=navigation, proper focus management, visible focus ring, screen-reader labels)
Performance: no added JS bundle > 40KB for nav logic; lazy-load heavy components like cost analytics
Analytics: nav_click, workspace_switch, deep_link_open events instrumented with route and workspace_id
design_decisions: Adopt compact vertical sidebar with icon+label; allow collapse to icon-only with tooltip on hover
Group secondary pages (billing, settings, API keys) into an expandable 'Admin' node to reduce top-level noise
Implement workspace switcher as a modalable overlay anchored to header avatar with inline search; also expose compact selector in sidebar for quick switching
Preserve last active sub-route per workspace in local storage and as parameter in the workspace switcher to support back-and-forth flows
Use route-first approach: navigation drives URL changes; components read route params for context rather than relying on global state
Introduce `router.suggestedFallback` mapping for older deep-links to redirect to new canonical routes (with 301-equivalent client behavior)
Prioritize keyboard navigation and screen-reader announcements during expand/collapse actions
engineering_notes: Routing changes require update to router-map v3 -> v4: add nested workspace param and route guards for SSO-only orgs
Server must expose /api/workspaces/:id/route_presets to resolve preserved sub-route; fallback to dashboards
Add feature flag `console_ia_v2` to gate release and enable A/B rollout; include telemetry toggles
Cost analytics component should be code-split and lazy loaded; show skeleton placeholder on nav click to maintain perceived perf
review_feedback: PM (Rosa Martinez): prefer keeping 'Models' top-level for quick access — move 'Deployments' under Models
Eng Lead (Marco Silva): ensure route guards don't add 200ms to first-load; suggested caching of workspace metadata
Accessibility (Priya Kapoor): ensure keyboard trap is removed when workspace modal closes; add live-region announcements
Security (Daniel Ng): confirm workspace switch respects SSO role-mapping; guest flows must not leak workspace names in URL previews
Support (Taylor Brooks): request an admin breadcrumb path in settings to help new reps find billing quickly

notes_for_engineers: Router changes should be backward compatible. Use client-side 302-style redirects with analytics tagging for migrated deep-links. Avoid global state for workspace context; prefer route params and small persisted 'lastRoute' per workspace.
summary: Console IA refresh ticket to redesign the main navigation and workspace switching experience. Prototypes exist; team aligned on compact sidebar + modal workspace switcher. Remaining work: accessibility fixes, router and backend support, and canary rollout planning.
